selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: S. 5046 prevents the Department of Education from moving specific offices and their duties to other federal agencies. It stops interagency agreements related to four major educational offices and mandates regular public reporting and cost analyses for existing or recent agreements, restricting travel funds if these reports are not submitted.

affected_groups.effect: Must halt interagency transfers of specified offices and functions, prepare detailed quarterly cost analyses and reports, and face travel funding restrictions if reporting requirements are unmet.

Programs, grants, oversight, and technical assistance associated with the four specified offices remain under the direct purview of the Department of Education rather than being transferred to other federal agencies.

key_provisions: Prohibits the Department of Education from entering into or carrying out interagency agreements with other federal agencies regarding four specific offices: the Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services, the Office of Postsecondary Education, the Office of Indian Education, and the Office of Elementary and Secondary Education.

Bans the transfer of functions such as grant administration, technical assistance, rule enforcement, data collection, and monitoring from the designated offices to other federal agencies or internally to other Department of Education offices prior to interagency transfer.
Excludes interagency agreements and arrangements that were already in effect on February 1, 2025, or renewals with substantially similar terms.
Requires the Secretary of Education to submit and publish detailed quarterly reports and cost analyses for any interagency agreement entered into on or after February 1, 2025.

Restricts the use of specific fiscal year 2026 and 2027 program administration and student aid administration funds for the Secretary of Education's travel expenses unless the required reporting is provided.
missing_information: The exact names or specific identities of the other federal agencies involved in the 14 interagency agreements entered into prior to the bill.
The total dollar amounts associated with the existing interagency agreements established on or after February 1, 2025.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 5046 prevents the Department of Education from moving specific offices and their duties to other federal agencies. It stops interagency agreements related to four major educational offices and mandates regular public reporting and cost analyses for existing or recent agreements, restricting travel funds if these reports are not submitted.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts the operational structure of the Department of Education by preventing the outsourcing or transferring of four major offices and their associated programs to other federal agencies, while enforcing strict transparency and financial reporting for recent interagency agreements.

title: A bill to prohibit the transfer of certain offices and functions of the Department of Education to other Federal agencies, and for other purposes.
